# Vlog or edited episode

After the clip, the viewer knows what happened in one scene: a place and what the people did there, a reaction and
what caused it, or a short story with its end.

## Finding the moment

- Rank the stretches by sound and picture together: a vlog's best scenes have something to see and something said or
  laughed at.
- A moment is one scene, from where it starts to where it lands: never a laugh without what caused it, never the
  middle of a walk where nothing is said or shown.
- A clip runs as long as its scene needs, up to 90 s: the length guessed is where to start, not where to stop.
  When a look ends before the scene lands (the answer to a joke, the laugh after it, the taste after the bite),
  look at the next stretch before you propose, and end after it (10-30, EP 22 ended at 25:56 while the table
  was building to a joke said at 25:58: "ตั้งชื่อร้านว่า ร้านเคี้ยวเอื้อง").
- Tell the person why the moment is worth watching by what happens in it: the place, what the people do or say.
- When the words heard in a stretch come out broken (another language, wind, music), judge it by its pictures, and
  tell the person the words could not be heard clearly.

## The clip

- Layout: the card, its whole height as its editor framed it. The program cuts its sides equally, as far as the
  faces in the moment allow, so the people and the subtitles an editor centres show bigger; a logo in a corner may
  go. Never cut the picture down to one face: a vlog cuts between shots, and a face is lost at every cut (10-29: a
  travel episode cut down to faces showed an eye and hair in the circles).
- Captions: plain captions of what is said. When the picture already has its own subtitles, put captions on anyway:
  the program leaves out each line said while the picture's own words show, because two sets of words fight, and
  draws none when they show over every line.
- The title names the place or what happens, in a few words, in the clip's language. It sits above the card, never
  over the picture's own subtitles.
- Look: none. The editor already chose the colours.
- Sounds: none. The vlog's own sound and music carry it.

## Checked at the end

- the captions are words that were said
- numbers on screen were said
- the length is inside the Reel limit, and the clip does not start silent or black

# The house standard

Every clip follows these rules, whatever its kind. They come from the short clips that worked: the format whose
clips reached 10,000 to 19,000 views, where the ones before it stayed under 1,100. Where this recipe says more about
its own kind, both hold; the person's own words win over both.

## The first two seconds

- Open on the clip's strongest line: the question it answers, the claim, the result or the peak. Never open on a
  greeting, a "today I will show you", a breath or a pause: viewers decide in the first two seconds, and a slow
  start loses them before the point.
- When the strongest line comes after a setup, start on that line and leave the setup out, as long as the clip still
  makes sense to someone who saw nothing before it.
- The title is on the picture from the first frame and tells the viewer why to keep watching.

## Cutting

- Each piece starts on the first word of a sentence and ends after its last word. Never cut words out so that
  someone seems to say what they did not say.
- One clip, one complete thought: a question and its answer with the numbers said, a step and its result, a story
  and its point.
- Nothing holds still for long: a still screen, such as a slide or a page, gets a slow push, and a number shows on
  the picture when it is said.

## Words on the picture

- The title and any big words are for a stranger scrolling past who knows nothing about the topic: everyday words,
  no jargon, no abbreviation they may not know. Say what the thing does for them: "บอทเทรด", not "EA"; "บัญชีทดลอง",
  not "Demo"; "ไม่มีจุดผิดเลย", not "compile ผ่าน". Captions stay the speaker's own words, jargon included.
- A title starts from what the viewer wants or what bothers them, in the words they would use, not from the name of
  a feature.
- A title reads right to someone who has not watched the clip. Join two things with จน, เลย or เพราะ only when the
  clip shows the one causing the other: "ทำกับข้าวบ้านเพื่อน ฮาจนต้องใช้หม้อ" glued a laugh to the pot in the
  episode's own subtitle, and nothing in the clip makes one cause the other, so it reads as nonsense.
- A number on the picture is exactly the one on the screen or the one said. When the hearing and the screen
  disagree, the screen wins. Never round, convert or guess a number.
- Claim only what the person said or the picture shows, never more, in the title, the cover, the post and the
  words on the picture. "ถ้าบ้านชื้นมาก เก็บสองวันก็เต็ม" was said; "บ้านชื้นแค่ไหนก็เอาอยู่" and "ลดเชื้อราได้จริง"
  were not, so they are made up. A viewer who buys on a claim nobody made stops trusting the channel.
- Never a middle dot (·) between phrases: a space, or a new line.
- Captions are plain when a person talks on camera. Words lit one by one only over a voice-over or a song: a moving
  colour under a talking face is a second place to look.
- Words never cover each other, a face, the product or a price.
- No sponsor's or brand's logo or name on the picture unless the person asks for it: a short cut loses the context
  that keeps it fair to them. A shop's or a place's name as its own sign writes it says where the viewer is, and
  may be named there.

## The post

- Never name another app, or use a tag that belongs to one, in the title, the post text, the hashtags or the words
  on the picture: the same file goes to every app. To point to the full video, write "ดูคลิปเต็มในลิงก์โปรไฟล์", or
  "full video: link in profile" in the clip's language.
- Five hashtags: first three about what the viewer is looking for or struggling with, because the apps show the
  first three; then two about the topic or the channel. Each one is about this clip: a tag any clip of its kind
  could carry says nothing.

## Hidden and kept

- The person's own name, on the screen or said, is kept: it is theirs to show.
- Hidden for as long as it shows: e-mail addresses, phone numbers, real account, card and ID numbers, other people's
  names on a screen, and folder paths that hold a user's name.

## Sound

- A game clip keeps the game's sound and the player's voice, with no music.

## Before handing over

- Watch the first two seconds once more as a stranger would: would they stop scrolling?
- Read every word on the picture as that stranger: is there a word they would not know? Say it another way.

features.ask: Use this clip's tagline and face circle on all the clips.

features.name: Take the album's look back
features.says: Takes the look you put across the album back off every clip, in one step.
features.ask: Take that look back off the other clips.

features.name: Update all videos
features.says: Makes the video again of each clip of the album that changed, one after the other.
features.ask: Update all the videos.

features.name: A tagline on the clip
features.says: Draws a short line of your words on the clip, at the bottom left, middle or right, or takes it off.
features.ask: Put the tagline Daily gold notes at the bottom right.

features.name: Open another clip
features.says: Opens another of the clips made in one go, so you can change it. The clip you leave keeps its changes.
features.ask: Open clip 3 and change its title.

features.name: Clips from a folder
features.says: Opens every short video in one folder, such as a day out shot on your phone, to make one clip from them.
features.ask: Make one clip from my Japan folder.

features.name: Tell it as a story
features.says: Puts the short videos in the order that tells the story best, keeps the best seconds of each, says why, and says why any was left out.
features.ask: Put my trip videos in a good order.

features.name: Top 5 countdown
features.says: Counts down the best moments of a game stream in one clip, the best last, each with its rank and a few words of what happens. In a football match it joins the goals in match order.
features.ask: Make a top 5 of the best moments in my stream.

features.name: Card layout
features.says: Your screen or game sits as a card across the middle, your face in a circle above it, and the captions between them, so nothing covers the picture.
features.ask: Put the game in the middle and my face on top.

features.name: Stacked layout
features.says: Your face on top and the game or screen below it, for a stream where your reaction matters as much as the game.
features.ask: Show my face on top and the game below it.

features.name: Full face
features.says: Your face fills the whole frame, for a story or a sit-down talk.
features.ask: Make it just me talking, full screen.

features.name: Follow the subject
features.says: One part of the picture fills the frame, such as the product in your hand or the action.
features.ask: Keep the product in the middle of the frame.

features.name: Frame follows the product
features.says: SAM 3.1 finds the product in every frame on this computer, and the vertical frame moves with it as you pick it up, turn it and put it down.
features.ask: Keep the frame on the controller as I move it around.

features.name: Move a part
features.says: Puts the face circle, the card, the captions or another part exactly where you want it, and says what a phone would cover there. On the page, tap anything on the clip and drag its frame.
features.ask: Move my face circle to the bottom right.

features.name: Pan inside a part
features.says: Changes what a part shows while the part stays where it is, such as the game further left in the card.
features.ask: Show more of the left side of the game in the card.

features.name: Who is on screen
features.says: In a talk between people, shows one person or everyone for a stretch, such as when someone reacts.
features.ask: Show her face when she laughs.

features.name: Plain captions
features.says: Captions of what was said, a few words a line, with every number exactly as said, so the eye stays on the picture.
features.ask: Add captions.

features.name: Lit-up captions
features.says: Each word lights up in colour at the moment it is said, like karaoke.
features.ask: Make each word light up as I say it.

features.name: Pop-in captions
features.says: Each word pops in at its place as it is said and stays, so the line builds up with the speech.
features.ask: Make the captions pop in word by word.

features.name: Clean words
features.says: Clear white letters with a thin dark outline that read on any picture.
features.ask: Use simple, clean text.

features.name: Bold pop words
features.says: Bold letters with a black outline and a shadow that stand out on busy game footage.
features.ask: Make the words bold so they pop on the game.

features.name: Sticker words
features.says: Dark letters on a white box, like a sticker on the clip.
features.ask: Put the words on white boxes like stickers.

features.name: Glowing script
features.says: Handwritten-style letters with a warm orange glow, for the one word that matters.
features.ask: Make the title glow.

features.name: 3D words
features.says: Heavy white letters with a deep orange edge and shadow, so they look raised off the clip.
features.ask: Make the title look 3D.

features.name: Classic italic
features.says: Elegant serif italic letters for short, calm words.
features.ask: Use an elegant italic font for the title.

features.name: Your font and colours
features.says: A font from the studio or from your computer, and your own colours; a colour that would be hard to read gets an outline that makes it readable.
features.ask: Use Kanit for the captions and make the title yellow.

features.name: Title on screen
features.says: Puts your words on screen for as long as you say, measured as they will be drawn, never over a face or where a phone covers the clip.
features.ask: Put 'Boss down' at the top for the first 3 seconds.

features.name: Fonts that fit
features.says: Lists the fonts that can write every letter of your words, Thai included, and whether each is free to use in a video you post.
features.ask: Which fonts can write Thai?

features.name: Take a title off
features.says: Takes a title off the clip by its words.
features.ask: Take the title off.

features.name: White flash
features.says: A short white flash on the moment something lands.
features.ask: Flash the screen when the boss goes down.

features.name: Screen shake
features.says: The picture shakes for a moment and settles, like an impact.
features.ask: Shake the screen on the hit.

features.name: Quick punch-in
features.says: A quick zoom in and back out, to punch a reaction.
features.ask: Zoom in fast on my reaction.

features.name: Big word
features.says: A big word such as POW pops in on the moment, grows past its size and settles, then fades.
features.ask: Put a big WOW when I win.

features.name: Slow push in
features.says: The picture moves slowly closer, like a camera pushing in, for the build-up before the peak.
features.ask: Slowly zoom in before the big moment.

features.name: Emoji sticker
features.says: A 3D emoji pops in, holds and fades out, such as fire on the peak or a money bag on a price.
features.ask: Add a fire emoji when I win.

features.name: Take off or move an effect
features.says: Any effect on the clip comes off or moves to another second, and the rest stays. On the timeline you can do the same by hand.
features.ask: Take off the shake, and move the fire to the end.

features.name: Picture of what you talk about
features.says: Muse Image draws a picture of a thing you name, such as a ghost in a ghost story, and shows it over the top of the frame for a few seconds, above the faces. Only your words go to Meta, never your footage. With your Meta key.
features.ask: When I talk about the ghost, show a picture of a ghost.

features.name: Sticker burst
features.says: A handful of stickers fly out from one spot every way, spinning, then drop a little and fade, like money thrown in the air.
features.ask: Make money burst out when I get paid.

features.name: Sticker rain
features.says: Stickers fall from the top one after another, swaying, such as coins raining down on a win.
features.ask: Make coins rain down when I win.

features.name: Sticker fountain
features.says: Stickers shoot up from the bottom and fall back, one after another, like a fountain.
features.ask: Shoot gems up like a fountain on the big moment.

features.name: Bouncing stickers
features.says: Stickers drop from the top, bounce twice on the bottom and stay there.
features.ask: Drop coins that bounce at the end.

features.name: Rising hearts
features.says: Stickers float up from the bottom to the top, swaying, like balloons or hearts.
features.ask: Float hearts up when I say thank you.

features.name: Scattered stickers
features.says: Stickers pop up one by one all over a box, stay a moment, then fade together.
features.ask: Pop fire and stars all around the title.

features.name: Party popper
features.says: Confetti and stickers shoot up from both bottom corners like a party popper, then drift down.
features.ask: Pop confetti when the clip ends.

features.name: Frosted glass box
features.says: A rounded frosted-glass panel, light or dark, for a title, a price or a list to stand on so the words read over a busy picture.
features.ask: Put the price on a glass box.

features.name: Vivid colour
features.says: More contrast and richer greens and blues, with skin and reds kept as they are: for games and flat footage.
features.ask: Make the colours more vivid.

features.name: Warm colour
features.says: Warmer middle tones with black and white kept, so a white product stays white: for faces, food and products.
features.ask: Make it look warmer.

features.name: Soft film look
features.says: Soft blacks and whites and calmer colour, for a quiet, calm clip.
features.ask: Give it a soft film look.

features.name: No chat box here
features.says: Tells the studio a game recording shows no chat box, so it asks for no blur. A viewer's name read on the screen still stops the clip.
features.ask: This is a console game, there is no chat.

features.name: Blur a box
features.says: Blurs one part of the picture so nothing in it can be read, such as the chat with viewers' names or a phone number.
features.ask: Blur the chat box.

features.name: Find someone in the clip
features.says: Shows the clip with a number on every face, so you can say who to blur by where they stand.
features.ask: Blur the man in white at 12 seconds.

features.name: Blur or keep people
features.says: You decide who is blurred and who is kept; a blurred face is followed as it moves. A clip with someone not yet decided is not made into a video.
features.ask: Blur the people behind me.

features.name: Words behind you
features.says: The title passes behind your head and body, so you stand in front of the words, and enough of them stays readable.
features.ask: Put the title behind me.

features.name: Black and white world
features.says: The footage around you turns black and white while you keep your colour; Meta's SAM 3.1 finds you frame by frame on this computer.
features.ask: Make everything black and white except me for the last 5 seconds.

features.name: Outline around you
features.says: A white edge follows your outline as you move, found by SAM 3.1 on this computer.
features.ask: Put a white outline around me when I laugh.

features.name: A new place behind a green cloth
features.says: Filmed in front of a green cloth? The studio cuts you off the cloth on this computer, and Muse Image draws a place behind you that suits the product, from words alone, never your footage. With your Meta key.
features.ask: Put a gaming desk behind me instead of the green cloth.

features.name: Hit sounds
features.says: A short sound on a moment: a deep thump, a whoosh, a pop or a small ding, used only on the hits that matter.
features.ask: Add a whoosh on the flash.

features.name: Your music
features.says: Your own music under the clip; it goes down while someone speaks, loops if short, and fades in and out.
features.ask: Put my song under the clip, quietly.

features.name: Mute a part
features.says: Pick the seconds and the sound there goes: a count-in, someone else talking, a noise. The picture and your music play on, and the captions leave out those words.
features.ask: Mute the sound from 0 to 3 s.

features.name: Choose sound tracks
features.says: When a recording holds several sound tracks, such as the game on one and your voice on another, every track is in the clip. Choose the ones you want.
features.ask: Use only sound track 2.

features.name: Your channel's look
features.says: Keeps this clip's text style, colour, captions, title spot and your channel's name, so every new clip starts in it. Save it under Channel beside the clip, or ask Muse.
features.ask: Save this look for my channel Sample Channel.

features.name: Switch channel
features.says: Puts one of your saved channel looks on the clip, or none.
features.ask: Use my Sample Channel look.

features.name: Undo
features.says: Takes the last change to the clip back. The Undo button under the clip does the same.
features.ask: Undo that.

features.name: Make the video
features.says: Makes the finished vertical video, 1080 by 1920, on your computer.
features.ask: Make the video.

features.name: Checks the facts
features.says: Checks the finished video for what a program can prove: captions are words that were said, numbers on screen were said, no viewer's name or private line can be read, it does not start black or silent, and it fits a Reel. The program checks facts; you keep the taste.
features.ask: Check the clip before I post it.

features.name: Cover by Muse Image
features.says: Muse Image turns the clip's best frame into its cover, with the title written big, the people and the product kept as you shot them. With your Meta key, one cent a cover.
features.ask: Make a cover for the clip.

features.name: Ready to post
features.says: Gives you the video with a title, post text and hashtags, a Copy all button and a download.
features.ask: Write the post text for Instagram Reels.
